title: Design System: Dash AI Open Source

display.purpose: The page h1 in Bricolage Grotesque 750, huge and tightly tracked.

headline.purpose: Section h2 headings in Bricolage Grotesque 750.

title.purpose: Register project names and spec-grid headings.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, ledes and controls in Geist.

label.purpose: Geist Mono for metadata terms, status badges, window titles, code and the copy button.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The shadow token is none; depth comes from 2px ink outlines, rules and band inversion.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: All transitions: button lift, row hover, logo slash, chip pop, sweep.

motion.name: theme-wipe
motion.value: 0.7s var(--ease), clip-path polygon along the -22deg slash

motion.name: survey-sent-sweep
motion.value: 0.9s var(--ease), skewed violet gradient crossing the form

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a printed broadsheet that happens to be interactive: black ink on white stock, enormous tightly tracked grotesque headlines, heavy rules that divide the page the way column rules divide a newspaper, and a single purple that appears only where the eye must land. The purple is the Dash AI slash. It is the one signal color, and the leaning slab-and-slash of the logo (a skew of -22 degrees) is the only gesture the system repeats: the closing band's block, the row-hover tick, the theme-switch wipe, the logo hover.

Density is calm and spacious. Content sits in a 1180px column with generous section padding, separated by rules rather than boxes. Real screenshots of the shipped tools are the only imagery, shown in window frames. Light and dark are both first-class; dark swaps ink and paper and brightens the purple, and the inverted bands flip with them.
keyCharacteristics: Black and white with one purple signal; everything else is a tint of ink.
Zero border radius on every surface and control.
Rules carry hierarchy: 2px ink under the header, 3px ink atop the project register, 1px hairlines between rows.
Display type is huge and tight (Bricolage Grotesque, 750); reading text is Geist; Geist Mono is for metadata and code.
Inverted full-bleed bands (black in light, near-white in dark) break the page's rhythm.
No cards: grids are divided by hairlines.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only chromatic color. It marks the action, the live state, and the slash; it is never used for large fills except the closing band's slash block.

rules.name: The Violet Ink Rule
rules.body: Violet as text uses Violet Ink (#5a1fd6 light, #b79bff dark); the bright violet is for fills and outlines.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: Inverted bands re-point the tokens (ink, soft ink, rules, surface) so every child stays legible; never hard-code a color inside a band.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is only for code, metadata terms, status badges, and window titles. It never sets headings or prose.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline tracking stays at -0.05em or tighter and line-height at or under 1.05; loosening it breaks the broadsheet voice.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and never lifted by a shadow; separation is a rule or a color inversion.

dos: Do use ink and paper for everything and reserve Slash Violet for the action, live state and slash.
Do build hierarchy with rules: 2px ink for major edges, 3px atop the register, 1px hairlines inside.
Do keep radius at 0 and shadows at none.
Do define every new color as a light/dark pair under `data-theme`.
Do show only real screenshots of shipped tools, in the window frame.
Do repeat the -22 degree slash as the only decorative gesture.
Do honor reduced motion: transitions and the entrance/wipe animations switch off.
donts: Don't introduce a second chromatic color or pastel tones.
Don't round corners or use pills.
Don't wrap content in cards; divide with hairlines.
Don't set headings in Geist or body copy in Bricolage Grotesque.
Don't use bright violet as small text on paper; use Violet Ink.
Don't invent projects, features or stats; only real tools appear.
